facts.text: I became unconscious at home and was brought to the emergency department.
I've been having spells of palpitations.
I get dizzy during my spells of palpitations.
I feel lightheaded during my spells of palpitations.
I sweat during my spells of palpitations.

facts.item: how long the spells have been going on
aliases: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: These spells have been happening over the past 2 months.
They often come on late after a meal, or after I've gone a long time without eating.

facts.item: low blood sugar during the spells
facts.text: When my blood sugar was checked during my spells of palpitations and dizziness, it went as low as 3.5 mmol/L, and it came up with glucose.
I haven't had any seizures.
I took high-dose dexamethasone tablets every day for a while.
The spells got better for a while, but they came back after I stopped it.
I've put on weight, but I don't know how much.
I've had trouble getting erections.
It's been going on for about a month.
No one in my family has had an insulinoma.
No one in my family has diabetes.
I haven't used any insulin.
For the past 2 months I've been injecting anabolic steroids for bodybuilding.
For the past 2 months I've been using growth hormone for bodybuilding.
For the past 2 months I've been taking amino acids by mouth for bodybuilding.
For the past 2 months I've been taking fat-burner supplements for bodybuilding.
I do bodybuilding.
Before all this I was healthy.

findings.result: As low as 3.5 mmol/L during the episodes; improved with dextrose.

gold.reasoning: 1. Adrenal insufficiency — “ACTH and nonstimulated morning cortisol levels were normal.” 2. Insulinoma — “MRI of the abdomen, including the pancreas, ... showed no abnormalities.” 3. Exogenous insulin administration — “the patient denied using exogenous insulin while proinsulin was below the reference range and the C-peptide level was normal.”

leakage.reason: Explicit family-history denial of insulinoma (a differential, not the gold); 'insulin' matches inside 'insulinoma'.
Explicit denial of exogenous insulin use from the source (s007); the word 'insulin' is unavoidable and names the drug, not the diagnosis.

source_issues: s012 calls the cortisol both 'random' and 'morning'; the reasoning calls it a nonstimulated morning cortisol.
The earlier capillary glucose nadir of 3.5 mmol/L is only mildly low, while the presentation value was <2 mmol/L.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation after he became unconscious at home with a capillary glucose <2 mmol/L, and the admission that followed (s001, s003-s009); the supervised fast, the laboratory tests during hypoglycaemia and the other tests and MRI (s010-s012) are findings of the same admission workup.
Finding names x010 'serum insulin' and x014 'anti-insulin antibodies' contain the gold word 'insulin' because these tests are named that way clinically; no neutral name exists.

The 2-month spells of palpitations, dizziness, lightheadedness and sweating share one duration and one timing (late after meals or after prolonged fasting), so these are standalone facts with general items.
Earlier glucose readings (s003) are a finding with time and also a medical_history fact, since the patient knows them.
